# rationale
The passage is a compact methods instruction: it tells the reader which outcomes to record, how to report them, what to pre-declare, and what conclusion not to draw. Nothing repeatedly interrupts it — there is exactly one closing caveat, and it sits where a guardrail belongs (after the requirements, before anyone acts on them). The real friction is not interruption but packing: a single sentence carries an eight-item, undifferentiated enumeration whose members sit at different levels of abstraction ("consequential false skips" vs. "subjective preference" vs. "unwarranted confidence"), followed immediately by three further procedural requirements in thirty-odd words. A reader has to hold the whole set in working memory before learning, in sentence three, what governs it. That is mild, structural compression rather than conceptual confusion, and a checklist format (or one item per clause) would relieve it without losing any content. The density itself is warranted: these are genuinely distinct dependent measures, and the qualification about denominators and the caveat about headline metrics are load-bearing, not defensive padding.
